summary.text: Sagittarius A*, or Sgr A*, is the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center of the Milky Way, and a bright, very compact astronomical radio source.
Astronomers weighed it using the orbits of nearby stars, especially S2, and the current best estimate of its mass is 4.297 million solar masses.
In May 2022 the Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of the accretion disk around its event horizon, the second confirmed black hole image after Messier 87's in 2019.

facts.label: Discovered
facts.value: In 1974, by Bruce Balick and Robert L. Brown

facts.label: Nobel Prize
facts.value: Genzel and Ghez each shared the 2020 Physics prize for it

facts.label: Why not visible
facts.value: Dust and gas absorb and scatter its visible light

items.prompt: Light cannot escape a black hole, yet astronomers have an image of the one at our galaxy's center. What does the picture show?

options.label: The surface of the object glowing from within
Hot gas and dust heated as it falls toward the object
A bright star sitting in front of the object
Starlight bent into a ring around the object

items.explain: The black hole itself is not seen. The observed energy comes from gas and dust heated to millions of degrees as it falls in.

items.prompt: How can astronomers weigh something at the galaxy's heart that they cannot see?

options.label: Measure how much visible light it blocks
Watch the orbits of stars circling it, such as S2
Count how many stars lie in the galaxy
Time flashes coming off its surface

items.explain: Observations of several stars orbiting Sagittarius A*, particularly S2, were used to determine its mass.

items.prompt: The Event Horizon Telescope found the source to be about 64 million kilometres across. Where does that fit among distances in our Solar System?

options.label: Smaller than Mercury's closest distance to the Sun
About the same as Earth's distance from the Sun
More than Mercury's closest distance, but less than Earth's
More than twice Earth's distance from the Sun

items.explain: Mercury is 46 million kilometres from the Sun at its closest and Earth is 150 million, so 64.1 million lies between them.

items.prompt: In 1982 Robert Brown put an asterisk in the name Sgr A*. What was behind that choice?

options.label: It marks a confirmed black hole, as opposed to a candidate
It flags a measurement that is uncertain
It shows the source seemed exciting, and atoms in excited states carry asterisks
It marks the brightest star in Sagittarius

items.explain: Brown coined the name because the radio source was exciting, and excited states of atoms are denoted with asterisks.

items.prompt: Two astronomers each won a quarter-share of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on our galaxy's core. What did they show?

options.label: That the center holds a tight cluster of dark stars and nothing more
That the center has no single concentrated mass at all
That the center is a supermassive compact object only a black hole explains
That relativity cannot explain how any black holes could form

items.explain: Genzel and Ghez were honoured for their discovery that Sagittarius A* is a supermassive compact object, for which a black hole was the only explanation.

items.prompt: Measurements from an aircraft-mounted camera in 2019 looked at the ring of gas and dust around Sagittarius A*. What did magnetic fields do there?

options.label: They pushed the ring outward, away from the black hole
They stopped the ring from emitting any light
They tore the ring apart into separate streams
They made the ring flow into orbit, which keeps the black hole's emissions low

items.explain: Magnetic fields cause the ring to flow into an orbit around Sagittarius A*, keeping black hole emissions low.
